title: Telex Watcher (external deterministic watch loops)
summary: The builder accepted the minimal command-plus-policy Watcher v2 contract for usability. The optional example pack is next-ready but unlaunched; runtime remains planned and blocked on Application Client client-conformance.

nodes.title: Vertical spike: generic external detector runner
nodes.summary: Build one provider-neutral persistent external watcher: trusted local detector commands, versioned structured results, opaque state, fixed Telex target/sender, state commit after durable send, restart recovery, and editable GitHub/Azure DevOps examples including repository-specific filtering. No agent session retains a background waiter.

nodes.title: External detector hosting is broadly useful
nodes.summary: Builder dogfoods materially different GitHub, customized GitHub, Azure DevOps, and non-PR watches. The gate passes only if agents can author detectors quickly, watches survive outside sessions, and Telex wakeup is more reliable and less disruptive than background loop tasks.

nodes.title: Production Watcher contract and application-client requirements
nodes.summary: Promote successful spike semantics into the intended design: detector envelope, watch lifecycle, script pin/follow policy, credentials and environment, failure notification, state/dedup transaction, service identity, message conventions, and the exact requirements exported to the shared Telex Application Client issue #12.

nodes.title: Minimal Watcher authoring and registration contract
nodes.summary: Completed through issue #133 and PR #135, merged as b91e830: command-plus-policy registration, detector request/result v2, runtime-generated event sequence identity, optional hardening, and ADR 0050's narrow supersession of ADR 0046.

nodes.title: Minimal Watcher contract is dumb and useful
nodes.summary: Builder accepts that an agent can write or copy a script and register command, bounds, and route without mandatory manifests, pinning, kind allowlists, provider preflight, downtime declarations, or a prescribed test framework.

nodes.title: Minimal Watcher runtime core
nodes.summary: Implement persistent registry and lifecycle, bounded scheduling/execution, v2 detector protocol, opaque state, runtime-generated event identity, fixed routing, receipt-gated commits, and attempt/health diagnostics under the accepted minimal contract.

externalDependsOn.label: Supported Application Client core/binding conformance accepted

nodes.title: Watcher CLI and diagnostics UX
nodes.summary: Provide add/list/show/pause/resume/update/remove plus concise status, attempt, state, and failure inspection so agents can register quickly and repair watches after execution.

nodes.title: Optional experimental v1 compatibility adapter
nodes.summary: If still valuable, provide an explicit compatibility/import path for spike-era v1 registrations and detector results without constraining the v2 product surface.

nodes.title: A custom watch is operational in five minutes
nodes.summary: Builder verifies a frontier agent can create a small customized watch in a few turns, register it without mandatory framework ceremony, leave it running after the session ends, and diagnose a failure from Watcher status and attempt/state surfaces.

nodes.title: Minimal optional detector examples
nodes.summary: Ship small copyable GitHub, Azure DevOps, HTTP/JSON, file, and command examples with short guidance, extracting selected PR #131 foundations without creating a mandatory template framework.

nodes.title: Optional Watcher hardening recipes
nodes.summary: Document optional project choices for Git pinning, digest checks, kind allowlists, provider preflight, cursor/downtime design, fixtures, and deeper tests without making them ordinary registration requirements.

nodes.title: Examples accelerate rather than constrain
nodes.summary: Builder verifies agents may use an example or ignore the pack and write a detector directly, and that examples reduce setup cycles without imposing a provider framework.

nodes.title: Watcher runtime reliability and packaging hardening
nodes.summary: Exercise restart/crash, malformed or hung scripts, output caps, many watches, SQLite/Postgres routes, diagnostics retention, packaging, upgrade, and operational recovery after the minimal UX and examples are accepted.

nodes.title: External watch loops reliably deliver Telex attention
nodes.summary: Builder validates several real long-duration watches, confirms session queues remain free of background waiters, accepts the minimal authoring UX and diagnostics, reviews hardening evidence, and accepts campaign integration with Operator Station.

checkpoints.title: Generic external Watcher proven valuable
checkpoints.summary: A provider-neutral detector loop works outside agent sessions and has been dogfooded across GitHub, Azure DevOps, and custom conditions.

checkpoints.title: Minimal Watcher authoring contract accepted
checkpoints.summary: The intended design supports command-plus-policy registration, agent-owned provider semantics, runtime-generated event identity, and optional hardening without a mandatory template framework.

checkpoints.title: Minimal Watcher runtime, CLI, and examples usable
checkpoints.summary: The supported client, minimal runtime/CLI, and optional examples let agents create, operate, and diagnose watches without session-owned polling or authoring ceremony.

checkpoints.title: Telex Watcher operationally validated
checkpoints.summary: Long-duration external observation and Telex event delivery have survived realistic reliability, security, packaging, and scale validation.
